text.p: Here are the main headlines from Lithuania's M-1 plus radio station's noon news report on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas today said he would not approve the controversial law on property restitution and returned the legislation to parliament.

Brazauskas said that the constitution was the most important issue and not the opinion of several people or political parties. This version of the law violates the constitutional rights of the citizens, he said.

- Estonian Prime Minister Mart Siimann said that his Lithuanian counterpart Gediminas Vagnorius misunderstood his comments about European Union applicants. Vagnorius said that Siimann's position was that geopolitical criteria should be used when determining EU membership. Siimann responded by saying that he meant that all candidates should be evaluated according to objective criteria. - The Vilnius session of the Joint Committee on the Free Trade Agreement between the European Union and Lithuania ends today. More than 40 officials from the European Commission and European Union member state representatives together with officials from Lithuanian government ministries discussed the fulfilment of the agreement, which was signed in 1995.
- Parliament plans to pass the law on company bankruptcy today and to change the law on the payments of salaries for members of parliament and government leaders.

- The Lithuanian constitutional court will decide today whether the government's decision, passed on August 31, 1995, about special auctions of government bonds, violated the constitution. The secret decision was passed in order to help two banks that later went bankrupt - Vakaru Bank and Aurabanka.
